```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#| echo: false
library(tidyverse)

tweets <- read_csv("data/tweets.csv")

```

## The Data
This data was taken from the Barack Obama Presidential Library created by the National Archives. The data set contains information about every Tweet made by Obama through the @POTUS44 handle. 

You can access the data for yourself here: [National Archives - Obama Tweets](https://www.obamalibrary.gov/digital-research-room/archived-white-house-websites-and-social-media)

```{r}
glimpse(tweets)
```

DATA Cleaning
```{r}
tweets2 <- tweets |> 
    mutate(
        timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp),
        text_lower = str_to_lower(text),
        text = str_replace_all(text, "&amp;", "&")
    )
```

## Text Analysis

#### Tweet Length
```{r}
tweets1 <- tweets2 |> 
    filter(!is.na(text)) |> 
    mutate(length = str_length(text_lower)) |> 
    mutate(mean = mean(length)) |> 
    mutate(length_ratio = length/mean) |> 
    select(length_ratio, length, tweet_id, timestamp, text, source) |> 
    arrange(desc(length))
tweets1 |> 
    summarize(mean = mean(length), max = max(length), min = min(length))
```

The mean length of the Tweets is 128 characters. This table displays the length of each post in descending order. Further, it takes the relative length of each post to the mean. The longest post had 171 characters, and the shortest Tweet contained only 17 characters. 

```{r}
tweets1 |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=timestamp, y=length)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.15,size=0.8, color = "#1DA1F2") +
    labs(title = "Length of Obama's Tweets Over Time", 
            x = "Date Posted", y = "Tweet Length (characters)") +
    theme_minimal()
```

#### Most common Hashtags
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    filter(is.na(retweeted_status_id), !str_detect(text, "^RT @")) |> 
    mutate(hashtag = str_extract_all(text_lower, "#\\w+")) |> 
    unnest(hashtag) |> 
    filter(!is.na(hashtag)) |> 
    group_by(hashtag) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    arrange(desc(n)) |> 
    slice_head(n=10) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=n, y = fct_reorder(hashtag,n))) +
        geom_col(fill = "#1DA1F2") +
        labs(title = "Top 10 Most Used Hashtags", x = NULL, y = "Hashtag")
```

This chart shows the 10 most highly used hashtags by former President Obama in his own Tweets. From this data, we can see that some of the issues he cared about includes climate action, healthcare, and equal opportunity. 

```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    filter(str_detect(text_lower,"#actonclimate\\b")) |> 
    mutate(month = floor_date(timestamp, "month")) |> 
    group_by(month) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=month, y = n)) +
        geom_line(color = "#1DA1F2") +
        labs(title = "Uses of #ActOnClimate Overtime", x = "Year", y = "Number of Uses")
```

This graph plots the usage of #ActOnClimate overtime in both Obama's own tweets and his retweets. The hashtag was introduced in the middle of 2013, peaking in usage towards the middle of 2014. It was used constantly in 2015 and dropped in usage towards the end of his second term.

#### tweets per month/ per year
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(month = month(timestamp, label =TRUE)) |> 
    group_by(month) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=month,y=n)) +
        geom_col(fill = "#1DA1F2") + 
        labs(title = "Obama's Tweets by Month", x = "Month", y = "Number of Tweets") 
```

This chart shows Obama's Tweets per month over the span of his time running the POTUS account. He has tweeted the most in January 
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(year = year(timestamp)) |> 
    group_by(year) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=year,y=n)) +
        geom_line(color = "#1DA1F2" ) + 
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2009:2016) +
        labs(title = "Obama's Tweets Over the Years", x = "Year", y = "Number of Tweets") 
```

```{r}
tweets2 |>
    mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
    group_by(date) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=date,y=n)) +
        geom_col() + 
        labs(title = "Obama's Tweets by Date", x = "Date", y = "Number of Tweets") 
```

This graph shows Obama's Tweets over his years in office. It shows that he used his Twitter more in his second term from 2013-2017, and used it the most in 2014 and 2015. This surge in usage in 2014 could be due to his decleration of the year as a "year of action," in which he enacted many executive orders and policy initiatives to address many issues of the time.

```{r}
tweets2 |> 
  mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
  count(date) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = n)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Obama's Tweets per Day",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of tweets")
```
```{r}
tweets2 |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(as_date(timestamp), "month")) |> 
  count(month) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + 
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Obama's Tweets by Month", 
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Number of Tweets") +
  theme_minimal()
tweets2 |>
  mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
  count(date) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 1) + 
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +

       x = "Year",
```
